rows.evidence: `modelRequestPermitProblem` is called only from `snapshotProblem` (model-request-codecs.ts:135, the store read validator registered at :216) and from the replay-event decode (:201); grep shows no other caller. A stored permit without `requestId` therefore needs a hand-edited/foreign or pre-decision-79 record; the service refusal at model-call-service.ts:65 is what a test can reach, not this codec arm.

rows.evidence: `deliveryPinProblem` has exactly one call site: the loop over `value['deliveryRefs']` at model-request-codecs.ts:97-100. The permit copies `inputBinding.deliveryRefs` (model-call-service.ts:148); the only production writers of the prepared input binding set it to `[]` (execution-preparation.ts:532 and :595) and `grep -rn deliveryRefs src` shows no other constructor. The manifest side also writes `[]` (execution-preparation.ts:532). Only a tampered/old permit can put an element into the loop, so the function body is unreachable and D2 (only-writer invariant) holds; the same evidence would read as U, but either way no platform writer produces the shape.
rows.proposal_note: Deleting the helper and loop is safe: one call site, no exhaustive switch depends on it, the field/type stays (contracts/dispatch.ts:307, model-call-contracts.ts:51), and no spec reserves Delivery pins (docs/refactor/tasks/B2-execution-state-skeleton.md:51 only declares the field; DESIGN.md:433 says never-written reference types were deleted and future records get new refs, so a later slice would define a new ref). Replacing the loop with an empty-array check is the strongest form; Codex's wording keeps only the outer `Array.isArray` check, which is equivalent today.

rows.evidence: `reworkPermission` is called first (requeue-service.ts:940-944) and refuses a non-active Goal (task-failure.ts:391-392) and a trigger from any actor but the canonical fan-out (task-failure.ts:420), so `goal.desiredState !== 'active'` can never be true at :951. The trigger is produced only by `findGoalResumeContinuations` from the same window read that returns the Goal (plan-service.ts:2235-2256; goal-machine.ts:652, :671), and the driver passes that read's Goal revision as the expected pin (goal-fan-out-driver.ts:444-459). requeue-service.ts:870-872 refuses any moved Goal revision first with the same `revision_conflict`. Equal pin therefore means the same Goal record, so `desiredStateRevision !== resumedEpoch` cannot be true either. Only a forged trigger sent with the platform fan-out identity could differ; that is actor impersonation, not a production caller path.
rows.proposal_note: Deleting :951-954 preserves behaviour: a moved Goal still yields `revision_conflict` at :870 and the driver's stale handling (goal-fan-out-driver.ts:472-479) still runs, while a non-active Goal is still refused `busy` at :940-944. Update the comment :945-947 and the GOAL-29 sentence (STATE-MACHINES-SPEC.md:396) to say the Goal pin carries the check. Residual for the lead: the Host actor id is not constrained (host.ts:318, main.ts:74-76), so an operator could start the Host as `host:goal-fan-out` and send a hand-made trigger through tasks/requeue (core-routes.ts:1113); the guard then answers instead of accepting, so if that identity should never be configurable, constrain the actor id rather than keep this branch.

rows.evidence: The reader drops human requeues (automatic-rework-notices.ts:178-179 via requeueActorClass :432-435). Every writer derives automation with `nextRequeueAutoCount` (requeue-service.ts:976; task-machine.ts:725, :1282), which sets `cap = policy.autoReworkLimit` (a number, contracts/task-requeue.ts:106) whenever the actor class is not human and `null` only for human (task-failure.ts:508-516). A requestedBy.kind==='agent' record is agent-class, hence automatic with a numeric cap. The requeue codec accepts `automatic:true, cap:null` (claim-record-codecs.ts:536-541), so only a hand-edited/old record reaches the return at :194; no platform writer produces it.
rows.proposal_note: Keep untested; the type (contracts/task-requeue.ts:156) still needs `number|null`, and the optional narrowing (a union keyed by `automatic`) is a code cleanup for the lead, not a test. No tamper test.

rows.evidence: `decodeCapOf` is called only for candidates read through the `s2a-round-reverify` index, whose path is `chain.reverify.actorClass` (evidence-record-codecs.ts:722-729); a root round has `reverify:null` (evidence-record-codecs.ts:260-276) so it never enters the index. The only successor writer, `commitReverify`, is called for a successor with `noticeAutomationCap: policy.autoReworkLimit` (evidence-service.ts:2028-2031) and writes it to the wire origin (:1698-1701); the cap-refusal path (evidence-service.ts:1961-1965) writes no successor round. Only a hand-edited or pre-T round without the wire field reaches :383; no current writer produces it.

rows.evidence: The record is re-read at decision-read-model.ts:1553 and decoded at :1555; a persisted `since:null` is already refused by decodeNoticeOrigin (decision-record-codecs.ts:394) and returned as unavailable at :1558-1560, so the `|| since === null` half of :1564 is dead. Creation always writes the `{since:null}` placeholder and binds it in the same commit (mailbox-service.ts:300-302; message-record-codecs.ts:1120 declares `since` as a commit-cursor field), and updates copy the stored origin, refusing an absent one (mailbox-service.ts:194-203, :2983). Only a hand-edited or pre-wiring message without `since` reaches the then arm; U stands.
rows.proposal_note: Codex's 'keep, no legacy sort fallback' and Claude's 'drop the dead null half' are both sound; dropping `|| since === null` is behaviour-preserving and keeping it is harmless. The `undefined` check stays untested (old/damaged record only, TP-063); no tamper test.
